investigations.name: blueprint-pipeline-fidelity
investigations.title: One blueprint, one pipeline: contract and t0 fidelity
investigations.objective: Can one versioned, backend-neutral blueprint be compiled by `blueprint_pipeline` and materialized faithfully on CPM, vertex and center-based, with the biological specification kept separate from backend and run parameters?
investigations.claim: ONE versioned, backend-neutral blueprint is compiled by the single `blueprint_pipeline` composite and materialized faithfully on the CPM, vertex and center-based backends. Design/Build half: the blueprint is a first-class artifact with a versioned schema, a canonical/backend split (backend and run parameters live in CompileOptions, never in the biological state) and a static validator with structured diagnostics. Simulate/ Evaluate half: the t0 state each backend actually emits matches the blueprint: 48/48 cell types, CPM centroid RMS 0.000 um, and a vertex sheet of 48 hexagons (36 epithelial + 12 immune attached at the tissue margin) with epithelial centroid RMS 1.60 um (max 2.44 um) and immune attachment RMS 4.11 um (max 5.60 um).

investigations.name: bounded-particles-cpm
investigations.title: Smoldyn particles bounded by Cellular Potts (CPM) voxel cells: confinement, conservation across division, reaction equilibrium
investigations.claim: A Smoldyn particle sim composed with the cpm backend keeps every cell's molecules strictly inside that cell's moving boundary (voxel-region outlines traced from the occupancy), conserves molecule count when a cell divides (each molecule inherited by exactly one daughter, by containment), and lets the reversible reaction A+B<->C reach equilibrium inside the living tissue.

investigations.name: bounded-particles-munk
investigations.title: Smoldyn particles bounded by center-based (viva-munk) discs: confinement, conservation across division, reaction equilibrium
investigations.claim: A Smoldyn particle sim composed with the munk backend keeps every cell's molecules strictly inside that cell's moving boundary (pymunk discs (oblong under crowding)), conserves molecule count when a cell divides (each molecule inherited by exactly one daughter, by containment), and lets the reversible reaction A+B<->C reach equilibrium inside the living tissue.

investigations.name: bounded-particles-vertex
investigations.title: Smoldyn particles bounded by tyssue (vertex) polygons: confinement, conservation across division, reaction equilibrium
investigations.claim: A Smoldyn particle sim composed with the vertex backend keeps every cell's molecules strictly inside that cell's moving boundary (junction-tension polygons), conserves molecule count when a cell divides (each molecule inherited by exactly one daughter, by containment), and lets the reversible reaction A+B<->C reach equilibrium inside the living tissue.

investigations.name: coupled-fate-oscillator
investigations.title: Coupled cell: an ODE metabolism and a MaBoSS fate network form a metabolism↔fate oscillator
investigations.objective: Can an SBML-ODE metabolism and a MaBoSS Boolean fate network be coupled inside one cell, in both directions, to produce a metabolism<->fate feedback oscillator that neither formalism shows alone?
investigations.claim: Two sub-cellular simulators of different formalisms — an SBML-ODE metabolism and a MaBoSS Boolean fate network — can be coupled inside one cell in both directions (the ODE's metabolite C pins the fate 'high_C' input, mode A; the fate 'divide' output resets the metabolism, mode C) to produce a metabolism↔fate feedback oscillator that neither formalism exhibits alone.

investigations.name: coupled-particle-catalysis
investigations.title: Coupled cell: a Smoldyn particle population catalyses an ODE (particle count sets the ODE rate)
investigations.objective: Can a Smoldyn particle population drive an ODE's kinetics inside one cell, so the ODE product accelerates as the particle count builds (mode B)?
investigations.claim: A Smoldyn particle simulator and an SBML-ODE can be coupled inside one cell so that the particle population drives the ODE's kinetics (mode B): the live count of a particle species sets the ODE's rate constant each step, so the ODE product accumulates faster as the particle population builds — a cross-formalism catalysis no single engine expresses.

investigations.name: coupled-triple-cell
investigations.title: Coupled cell: all three sub-cellular formalisms and all three coupling modes in one cell
investigations.objective: Can one cell run all three sub-cellular formalisms at once, coupled by all three modes (particle->metabolism->fate->reset)?
investigations.claim: A single cell can run all three sub-cellular formalisms at once — a Smoldyn particle sim, an SBML-ODE metabolism and a MaBoSS fate network — coupled by all three modes simultaneously: the particle count catalyses the metabolism (B), the metabolite pins the fate input (A), and the fate output resets the metabolism (C).

investigations.name: cross-paradigm-equivalence
investigations.title: Cross-paradigm equivalence: fate yes, exact position no, and the test has power
investigations.objective: Under replication, are the three mechanical substrates EQUIVALENT (not merely "not-distinguishable") on cell fate and on exact spatial position when one backend-neutral blueprint is run through `blueprint_pipeline`, and does the test correctly REJECT when mechanics (not the shared mechanism) drives the outcome?
investigations.claim: Run through `blueprint_pipeline` on CPM, vertex and center-based (viva-munk), the ONE Sego 2022 blueprint gives backend-neutral cell FATE and backend-specific exact POSITION, and the equivalence test is powerful enough to tell them apart. FATE agreement is statistically EQUIVALENT for every backend pair within a pre-declared +/-0.05 margin (run-cluster 90% CI [-0.0034, +0.0008] for cpm-vertex). Exact-position agreement is NOT equivalent for any pair at +/-0.10, and it orders by how different the geometries are: cpm-munk +0.093 < cpm-vertex +0.126 < vertex-munk +0.252 (the cpm-munk point estimate sits below the 0.10 margin but its CI [0.034, 0.159] does not fit inside +/-0.10, so equivalence still cannot be claimed). A mechanics-dominated positive-control arm REJECTS equivalence for every pair with the same test (cpm-vertex Delta +0.325), so a "pass" on fate is informative. Judged against the same-backend seed null, the N=400 capstone fate metric fails to reject a substrate difference, while infected-patch occupancy IoU and patch location now sit outside both same-backend baselines for the current vertex substrate: a candidate substrate signal, not causally attributed.

investigations.name: dose-response-crossparadigm
investigations.objective: Do the two substrates agree on the SIGN of the dose response over initial viral load (more load -> more infection), robustly across seeds?
investigations.claim: RE-RUN 2026-11-05 on the in-sheet immune vertex substrate (re-calibrated motility): figure regenerated; the STRICT-DIRECTION behavior test (highest dose ends with more infection than the lowest, on both backends) still passes. Earlier reading:   Both backends agree on the DIRECTION of the dose response: a HIGHER initial viral load (more initially-infected epithelial cells) ends with STRICTLY more infection than a LOWER load, on every backend and seed tested. This is a directional (lowest-vs-highest) result; intermediate-dose monotonicity is seed-dependent and is NOT claimed.

investigations.name: fateful-tissue
investigations.title: Fateful tissue: a dividing tyssue whose divisions are decided by each cell's own metabolism→fate chain
investigations.objective: Can a dividing tissue's divisions be decided by each cell's own metabolism->fate chain, with confined particles that split on division — composing every scale at once?
investigations.claim: Every scale this workspace can simulate composes into one system: a tyssue of dividing cells, each running a Smoldyn particle sim confined to its moving polygon (split on division) AND an ODE metabolism whose metabolite pins a MaBoSS fate network — and the fate 'divide' output DRIVES the tissue division. Cells grow as they metabolise (target area tracks the metabolite), divide when their own fate fires, and daughters reset and regrow, so the tissue sustains. Biology decides when the tissue divides.

investigations.name: scene-model-mixed-formalism
investigations.title: Model-definition format: one scene, three cell types, three formalisms (ODE, Smoldyn particles, MaBoSS) sharing an extracellular field
investigations.claim: A declarative scene (cells + types) bound to a per-type model registry compiles to one composite in which metabolic cells run an SBML-style ODE, signalling cells run Smoldyn particles and fate cells run a MaBoSS Boolean network, all coupled to a shared extracellular field through typed membrane transport.

investigations.name: subcellular-layer-grow-divide
investigations.title: Subcellular ODE layer: cells grow and divide on every backend
investigations.objective: Does the pluggable per-cell subcellular (tellurium ODE) layer grow AND divide cells uniformly across cpm, vertex and munk through `blueprint_pipeline`?
investigations.claim: The pluggable per-cell subcellular layer (a tellurium ODE bound to a cell type in the v2 blueprint) grows AND divides cells uniformly across CPM, vertex and center-based through the single `blueprint_pipeline`. In the demo blueprint a nutrient field sampled at each cell's centroid drives a per-cell growth ODE; the ODE species S actuates target_size (cells grow) and crossing the divide threshold triggers division with a lineage entry on every backend. Cell-count progressions in the 12-step e2e run: CPM 4 -> 8 -> 16, vertex 4 -> 8 -> 16, center-based 4 -> 6 -> 8 -> 16. This is a demonstration of the wiring (blueprint -> pipeline -> per-cell ODE -> backend actuation), not a biological result.

investigations.name: substrate-behavior-at-scale
investigations.description: HOW THE VERTEX MECHANICS WERE MATCHED (methods; evidence in results/vertex_mechanics_calibration.json, script scripts/calibrate_vertex_mechanics.py, full term-by-term definition in docs/mechanics.md). Both substrates' mechanics are written out term by term with every per-cell-type and per-type-pair parameter. CPM contact energy J (per neighbour bond) and vertex junction tension Lambda (per unit length) both penalize interface; the area constraint lambda_V (V - V_T)^2 and the area elasticity K/2 (A - A0)^2 are the same energy up to K = 2 lambda_V; the CPM temperature T drives membrane fluctuations and wandering that the deterministic vertex model must get from active (motility) forces; tension contracts cells against area elasticity, so the tension scale sets the relaxed area. Every vertex parameter is then either (i) energy-matched to its CPM counterpart (area stiffness K = 2 lambda_volume, per cell type), (ii) lowered per type PAIR from the blueprint adhesion table (Lambda_ab = kappa * J_ab, ratios fixed by J, the full per-pair table applied), or (iii) CALIBRATED to measured CPM behaviour on the Sego initial state under a hard mesh-validity constraint (no folded faces). Calibration drives each backend directly from the Sego initial state with no field / rule / ODE inputs (60 steps x 5 seeds) and fits, one observable each: tension_scale -> mean epithelial area; motility -> latent-immune random-walk displacement; sheet_motility -> epithelial MSD about the sheet centre, then CAPPED (stepped down by 0.8x) until a 3-seed x 400-step run has no inverted or self-intersecting face; tension_noise -> area CV (adopted only if it beats no noise by > 0.01 AND keeps the mesh valid); migration_scale + chemotaxis_saturation -> one active macrophage's drift speed vs a fixed linear virus gradient (g = 0.001 .. 0.03). The tension_scale sweep is re-run on the 4x4 mechanics-only sheet (workspace/blueprints/mechanics_sheet.yaml, 60 steps, reconnection on) and epithelial neighbour exchanges are counted on the Sego sheet over 400 steps. Other vertex-side stabilizers: auto_reconnect on (T1 at 0.1-0.2 x hexagon side, p_4 = 1), explicit Euler stabilized (viscosity 2 K A0, 4 sub-steps per coupled step; at viscosity 1 the displacement clamp was masking an oscillation), and the domain is a wall as on the CPM. Result: area, immune motility and the saturating chemotactic drift are matched (area 22.97 vs 22.98; immune displacement matched in the 2026-10-28 calibration, 9.36 vs 9.37 um); epithelial wandering and area dispersion are NOT matched, because every CPM-matching sheet motility folds the mesh and is therefore capped. Once the per-pair tension is actually applied, junction tension sets the relaxed cell area, so the J<->Lambda scale is identifiable (but geometry-dependent); without a temperature the vertex model needs active motility to wander, and a tyssue sheet absorbs only limited active shear before polygons fold -- a real limit of this substrate at these parameters.
investigations.title: Substrate behavior at scale: distance-to-CPM, and how the vertex mechanics were matched
investigations.objective: Now that center-based (munk) cells move and interact and the tissue is large enough for real spatial dynamics, which substrate reproduces the CPM's interaction pattern, and on which axes does each diverge?
